# Sambhavajātaka (Ja 515)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

According to the traditional nidāna, the Buddha recounted this story while dwelling at Jetavana in connection with the Perfection of Wisdom (*paññāpāramitā*), with the full introductory circumstances cross-referenced to the *Mahāummagga Jātaka* [Fausböll 1891].

Set in Indapatta in the Kuru kingdom during the reign of King Dhanañjaya-koravya, the narrative centers on the king's royal counselor, the brahmin Sucīrata (identified as a past birth of Anuruddha), who is asked by the monarch how a ruler can unite justice and advantageous actions [Nyanaponika et al. 2003; Fausböll 1891]. Lacking intellectual pride, the brahmin acknowledges his inability to resolve the dilemma and diligently searches for an answer until he encounters the Bodhisatta [Nyanaponika et al. 2003]. The Jātaka commentary cites the *Sambhavajātaka* alongside texts like the *Sarabhaṅgajātaka* to illustrate the pre-eminence of the power of wisdom (*paññābala*) [Fausböll 1891]. The narrative also appears in epigraphic records of early Pagán in Burma, where associated names like Yudhitthila are attested [Luce et al. 1970], and is mentioned in the *Sāriputtattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 3).

 DharmaNexus detects near-complete textual overlap with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (99 matches totaling over 12,800 shared characters) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments identified by DharmaNexus show substantial shared material in Sanskrit with the *Saṅghabhedavastu* (33 matches, scores up to 85), as well as verses shared with the *Udānavarga* and Avalokitasiṃha's *Dharmasamuccaya* [DharmaNexus]. Additional alignments appear in Tibetan canonical literature (including the *Vinayakṣudrakavastu* and *Karmaśataka*) and Chinese canonical texts, specifically the *Ekottarika-āgama* (T 125) and T 8 (*Dà jiāngù póluómén yuánqǐ jīng*) [DharmaNexus].
